forecasts.claim: Watch gas and diesel prices, not oil.

state_history.reason: The first-party Substack note title establishes a bounded comparative attention claim: watch gas and diesel prices rather than crude oil. The embedded video has not yet been transcribed, so the purpose and prediction horizon remain unresolved.

Official EIA data show diesel accelerated after July 13 while distillate inventories remained below their five-year average; BLS July data show substantial year-over-year energy inflation but mixed monthly CPI/PPI/freight direction. This supports testing refined products as an informational signal but does not by itself establish that they outperformed crude oil as a predictor for the specific outcome Randolph intended.

forecasts.calibration_notes: This is currently an indicator-selection claim, not yet a fully specified quantitative forecast. Resolution requires the embedded video/transcript plus a predeclared comparison target: consumer inflation, freight costs, product shortages, refinery margins, or another stated outcome.

limitations: The embedded July 13 video has not yet been transcribed or independently preserved.
The title alone does not specify which downstream variable gas/diesel should predict or how predictive superiority over crude should be measured.
A rising diesel series does not itself prove causal transmission to inflation or freight prices.
Comparative predictive performance against crude oil requires a fixed target, lag structure, and scoring rule defined before resolution.
No aggregate credibility finding is authorized from this record.
